sec:hadron-algebra-intro: The quark and pair-production relations of the preceding section single out those multi-strand configurations in H_n(q) that bind into colour-neutral composites. This section defines a hadron as a closed braid composite whose Coulomb charge and crossing energy lie in the stability stratum of the relation algebra, defines the proton \mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d}) as the first example, proves existence and uniqueness of minimal-energy normal-form representatives up to braid isotopy, and shows that confluent Gröbner–Shirshov reduction factorizes any closed strand uniquely into hadron constituents in the Pawlowski–Leitner basis. Equipping a hadron with a marked localization point on its Bring fibre prepares the knot–particle correspondence of the next section.
def:hadron:
Definition Hadron (stable knot composite). Let K_1, \ldots, K_n be prime knot types in the representation category \mathbf{C}. Let \mathcal{L} be a link encoding their internal entanglement. A hadron is a composite

  \mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}

satisfying the stability condition:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}_p) < 0.

The subscript p specifies the localization point. The operator \oplus denotes linking.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. Categorical identities hold over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
def:categorical-proton:
Definition Proton (categorical). The proton is the baryon governed by the 2 + 1 crossing partition: two up quarks (positive orientation) and one down quark (negative orientation) bound within the Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3.

  \mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d})

where:

  • \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 is the Borromean braid of three unknots threaded through color tubes (r,g,b). Two unknots bear positive crossing orientation (\mathfrak{u}) and one bears negative orientation (\mathfrak{d}).
rem:categorical-proton-properties:
Remark Proton: NF construction, mass, charge, and computational backing. The proton definition establishes the \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d}) baryon. One derives its normal form, mass, Coulomb charge, and computational backing.

Step 1: Borromean braid NF. The inverse relation \sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_1 - h_{\mathrm{A}} \mathbf{1} yields \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0(\sigma_1 - h_{\mathrm{A}}))^3. Expanding and reducing within H_3(q) gives \mathrm{net}(\mathcal{B}_3) = +1.0000. The terms L_\pm manifest the gluon field.

Step 2: Typed crossings. Quark flavor rigidly specifies the crossing eigenvalue. The \mathfrak{u}-\mathfrak{u} crossing preserves the eigenvalue +q. The \mathfrak{d}-type crossings impose a full -h_{\mathrm{A}} shift. Mixed \mathfrak{u}-\mathfrak{d} crossings incur a half-shift -\tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}.

Scope of the LP stability constraint. Under the Markov-recursion evaluation \mathrm{tr}_M(e^-) = h z^2 + z (rather than the retired ansatz \mathrm{tr}_M(e^-) = z^3), the bare nine-crossing element \mathcal{B}_3 \times \Delta_3(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) has \mathrm{tr}_M = +0.544 > 0, and every intermediate step of the typed build also maintains positive trace. Consequently, the bare nucleon already lies inside the Frobenius-positive feasible set without requiring a gluon L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 to repair a sign violation; whether the gluon stabilizer is forced by an independent variational constraint remains open.

What survives unchanged is the scope of the enumeration. The integer LP dual enumerates all feasible gluon combinations and selects the configuration minimizing |\mathrm{tr}_M|. That enumeration ranges over every non-trivial braid word inside the crossing cap, not over L_\pm alone. The electron word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is inside the range and is admissible; it is not selected because it loses the minimisation, not because anything forbids it.

Step 3: Proton NF. Applying typed crossings and gluon stabilisation yields \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{p}) = +1.0065. The dominant term is e^- \approx +1.022. The Hopf gluon link actively redistributes normal-form weight from \sigma_1 into the e^- channel.

Mass. The proton mass derives from the muon-anchored Hecke energy of the Borromean braid:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} =
  2\,\bigl(\mathfrak{m}_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 6\, m_e\bigr) +
  \text{Skein corrections},
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{m}_\mu = m_e\,\frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2},
  \quad
  F_{\mathrm{Bor}} = \lvert\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})\rvert\,\frac{[3]_q!}{q^3}.

The hyperbolic-volume dependence enters through the muon anchor \mathrm{Vol}(4_1), dressed by the dimensionless Borromean factor F_{\mathrm{Bor}}.

The Skein corrections isolate the crossing asymmetry between the \mathfrak{u} and \mathfrak{d} components. The pair Skein formula dictates \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} = \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}}(q) + 2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}}(q).

Gluon content and colour symmetry. The Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 natively carries Hopf link content; this constitutes the intrinsic gluon field binding the components. The S_3 permutation symmetry of the color tubes guarantees the invariant structure across all color assignments.
prop:hadron-exists:
Proposition Existence of hadrons. There exists a composite \mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L} satisfying the stability condition \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}_p) < 0.

Uniqueness of the hadron at a given crossing partition is established subsequently.
prf:hadron-exists: Proof Proof of existence of hadrons. The proton \mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) (categorical proton) provides a witness hadron. Its crossing energy is negative at the aether value q_0. LP-stability analysis on the Hecke basis confirms this. The Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 combined with gluon stabilization ensures \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p}) < 0. Similar constructions yield the neutron \mathfrak{n} and other hadrons. \square
prop:hadron-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of hadrons up to braid isotopy. Two hadrons sharing a crossing partition, localisation point p, and Hecke normal form coincide up to braid isotopy.

The Hecke normal form furnishes a canonical representative. Thus, uniqueness denotes uniqueness of the Hecke class in the algebra H_n(R, q).
prf:hadron-unique: Proof Proof of uniqueness of hadrons up to braid isotopy. Two braids representing hadrons with identical crossing partitions are equivalent in H_n(R, q) if and only if they share a Hecke normal form. The Markov trace provides an isotopy invariant \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = J_L(q). Braid isotopy preserves the Hecke class. For hadrons with identical partitions and localisations, Gröbner–Shirshov reduction guarantees a canonical normal form representative. This representative is unique in H_n(R, q). Therefore, the Hecke normal form completely determines the hadron up to isotopy.
rem:hadron-interpretation:
Remark Stability condition and abstract character of the hadron. Arbitrary knot composites are not stable. Only composites whose R-matrix braiding yields net binding qualify as hadrons. The Coulomb charge Q(\mathfrak{H}) measures the electromagnetic character of this composite.

The integer n counts the constituent knots and defines the valence. A valence of 3 yields a baryon; a valence of 2 yields a meson.

This definition remains abstract. The Euler characteristic \chi(A) in the Descartes universe dictates the specific torus knots serving as generators.

Stability as binding. A hadron is a stable composite of fundamental knots: its crossing energy is strictly negative, so topological binding dominates repulsion.

Localized hadrons. A localized hadron is a hadron placed at a categorical point p of the projective line \mathbb{P}(V); the morphism distinguishes it from an abstract one.
prop:hadron-operations-closure:
Proposition Closure of hadron operations under braiding, Hopf linking, skein action, and fusion. Let \mathbf{C} be a rigid braided monoidal category and let \mathfrak{H} \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) be a hadron with constituent knots K_1, \ldots, K_n.

  1. Braiding closure. The braiding \beta_{K_i, K_j} descends to an involution on \mathrm{Sym}^n(K). For the antisymmetric product, exchanging identical constituents produces the sign
  \beta_{K_i, K_i}\big|_{\mathrm{alt}} = -1 .
  1. Hopf linking closure. The linking operation \ell_{ij} \colon K_i \otimes K_j \to K_i \mathbin{\#_{\mathrm{Hopf}}} K_j is an endomorphism of \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} with a two-sided inverse when the linking number is trivial.
  2. Skein closure. The q-deformed skein relation resolves any linked composite into a polynomial in q times unlinked constituents, yielding the mass formula
  \mathcal{M}(\mathfrak{H}) = Q(q) \cdot \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) + \sum_i \mathcal{M}(K_i).
  1. Fusion closure. For hadrons \mathfrak{H}_1 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_1}(K) and \mathfrak{H}_2 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_2}(K), the fusion \mathfrak{H}_1 \star \mathfrak{H}_2 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_1 + n_2}(K) is again a hadron, with associative constituent composition across (n_1 + n_2) + n_3 and additive mass \mathcal{M}(\mathfrak{H}_1 \star \mathfrak{H}_2) = \mathcal{M}(\mathfrak{H}_1) + \mathcal{M}(\mathfrak{H}_2).
rem:hadron-operations:
Remark Operations on hadrons. The braiding and Hopf link structure of \mathbf{C} induce natural operations on the symmetric product \mathrm{Sym}^n(K).

Braiding. The braiding \beta_{K_i, K_j} permutes constituent knots within a hadron. Because \mathrm{Sym}^n quotients by the symmetric group action, this descends to an involution.

Hopf linking. Two knots link via the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}. The linking operation replaces two constituents with a linked pair. The inverse decomposes a linked pair when the linking number is trivial.

Skein action. The q-deformed Skein relations act on \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} by resolving link crossings. Iterating across all crossings resolves the composite into unlinked constituents scaled by a polynomial in q.

Fusion. One fuses two hadrons by constructing the Hopf link between their binding structures. This provides a categorical model for hadron scattering.
rem:knot-factorization:
Remark Knot factorization through tensor powers of V. The tensor generation property of the fundamental object V implies every constituent knot type K_i factors through a tensor power of V.

If K_i has associated simple object V_{j_i}, then V_{j_i} appears as a direct summand of V^{\otimes 2j_i}. The Pawlowski--Leitner basis provides a canonical embedding, so a hadron \mathfrak{H} can be written in a universal tensor form:

  \mathfrak{H}  \hookrightarrow 
  V_{1/2}^{\otimes 2(j_1 + \cdots + j_n)}.

This embedding corresponds to a choice of partial-wave channel. The physical hadron is obtained by summing over all channels weighted by the Skein polynomial.

In the QOU framework, this factorization explains why all composite particles are built from V. The categorical dimension 2 of V is the minimal non-trivial dimension compatible with the volume constraint.
def:localized-hadron:
Definition Localized hadron. Let p be a categorical point of the projective line \mathbb{P}(V). A localized hadron at p is a morphism in \mathbf{C}:

  H_p  \colon  \mathbf{1}
   \longrightarrow 
  \mathrm{Sym}^n\!\bigl(\mathcal{K}_p\bigr)
  \otimes
  \mathcal{L}_{p}^{\mathrm{bind}}

where \mathcal{K}_p denotes the fibre of knot types at p and \mathcal{L}_{p}^{\mathrm{bind}} is the binding Hopf link at p.
def:hadron-fibre-embedding:
Definition Fibre-compatible hadron embedding. Let \mathfrak{H} \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} be a hadron. Let \mathcal{S}_p denote the fibre over a point p \in \mathbb{P}(V). A fibre-compatible hadron embedding is a morphism

  \iota_p \colon \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} \longrightarrow \mathcal{S}_p

satisfying four conditions.

  1. Integrability. The abstract Skein action intertwines with the geometric operations on knots in \mathcal{S}_p.
  2. Fibre confinement. The image \iota_p(\mathfrak{H}) lies entirely in \mathcal{S}_p.
  3. Hopf compatibility. The embedding respects the Hopf structure.
  4. Volume compatibility. The embedding preserves hyperbolic volumes: \mathrm{vol}(\iota_p(K_i)) = \mathrm{vol}(K_i).

A localized hadron with a fibre-compatible embedding is a physically realized hadron.
rem:hadron-fibre-embedding-remark:
Remark Why hadrons embed in the geometric fibre. Abstract hadrons encode topological data algebraically. To represent a physical particle, this data must embed into the geometric fibre of the knot bundle over spacetime; a fibre-compatible hadron embedding is that embedding.

The fibre-confinement condition is enforced by a finite Möbius energy bound, preventing the knot complement from developing cusps that reach the fibre boundary. The integrability condition ensures the algebraic structure admits a strict geometric realization.
sec:skein-particle-generation-intro: Under the quadratic Hecke skein relation \sigma_i - \sigma_i^{-1} = (q - q^{-1})\mathbf{1}, every factorized hadron resolves into a linear combination of torus knots and links T(m, n) together with Borromean three-strand closures. This section constructs the atomic braid \mathcal{A}(Z, N) \in H_{A+Z}(q), proves that the torus family T(m, n) generates the hadron monoid under skein resolution and linking operations, and tabulates the resulting knot–particle dictionary across the lepton, meson, baryon, and gauge sectors.
def:atomic-braid:
Definition Atomic braid H_{A+Z}(q). The atomic braid of a neutral atom (Z, N) is the element of H_{A+Z}(q) obtained by assembling Z protons, N neutrons, and Z electrons into a single Hecke algebra with A + Z strands, where A = Z + N. The crossing coefficients are:

See Table 1.

The ground-state ordering is determined by:

  1. Nuclear ordering: minimize \Phi_1 over all permutations of Z protons and N neutrons.
  2. Electron insertion: greedily insert each of Z electrons at the position minimizing \Phi_1.

Combinatorial complexity of clause 1. Clause 1 quantifies over all \binom{A}{Z} distinct nucleon arrangements, so its full enumeration grows exponentially in A (\binom{12}{6} = 924 for {}^{12}\mathrm{C}, whereas \binom{40}{20} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{11} for {}^{40}\mathrm{Ca}). Clause 2 is greedy and therefore polynomial in Z, whereas clause 1 is not. No heuristic polynomial restriction is substituted into the definition itself; any computation evaluating a ground-state ordering for A \gtrsim 14 restricts the search space of clause 1 and specifies the chosen restriction explicitly.

The greedy insertion produces ep pairs: each electron sits immediately before its proton. The \mathfrak{n}e = \mathrm{id} crossing means electrons pass through neutrons without generating Hecke generators.

The atomic braid carries the electron shell: the three electronic rows of Table 1 — \mathfrak{p}e, \mathfrak{n}e, ee — are part of the definition, not an optional dressing. It is therefore a different object from the electron-free nuclear core \mathcal{B}_K \in H_{3A}(q), which places three quark strands on each nucleon and carries no electron content (notation register). The two are not two conventions for one braid: H_{A+Z}(q) cannot contain a word on 3A strands at any A, since A + Z < 3A whenever Z \geq 1. The symbol \mathcal{A} denotes the atom defined here; an element of H_{3A}(q) is written \mathcal{B}_K.

For hydrogen (A = 1): the bare [e, \mathfrak{p}] braid is LP-unstable. The \mathfrak{p}e crossing uses the \mathcal{B}_3-dressed eigenvalues (q^5, -q^{-5}) instead of the bare (q^{-1}, -q).

def:knot-particle-generation:
Definition Knot-particle generation from T_{m,n} torus knot generators. The particle spectrum is generated from a finite set of torus knot generators T_{m,n} (with \gcd(m,n) = 1) embedded in the standard torus \mathbb{T}^2 \subset S^3, together with two linking operations that act on the exceptional divisor and the color-tube fibration. The torus knot generators are the family

  \mathcal{G} =  \bigl\{ T_{m,n}  \big| 
  \gcd(m,n) = 1, m < n,
  m + n \leq N(\chi) \bigr\},

where T_{m,n} winds m times around the meridian and n times around the longitude of \mathbb{T}^2, and N(\chi) is a cutoff determined by the Euler characteristic of the Frobenius--Hopf object. For the Descartes universe with \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6, the bound is N(-6) = 9, admitting:

See Table.

One reserves q for the aether parameter and p for base points. The winding indices are always (m,n).
def:linking-operations: Definition The two geometric linking operations. The two linking operations are the geometric operations that build composite knots from the torus knot generators: (i) Hopf linking on the exceptional divisor, and (ii) color-tube threading of the color-tube fibration.

rem:knot-particle-generation-consequence:
Remark Boson links, zero hyperbolic volume, and the Skein-module presentation. The fermion--boson decomposition extends the generator set to the even-n torus links, which represent bosons. These include the T(2,2) gluon, the T(2,4) W boson, the T(2,6) Z boson, and the T(2,8) Higgs boson. These are two-component links with \gcd(2,n) = 2, carrying integer spin.

All torus knots have zero hyperbolic volume. Thurston's trichotomy sorts every knot into torus, satellite, or hyperbolic; torus knots are their own class, and only the hyperbolic class carries a volume. Consequently, their bare mass under the topological mass formula vanishes:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{bare}}(T_{m,n}) = 
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(T_{m,n})}{\hbar_q^{2}} =  0.

Mass arises entirely through the linking operations: Hopf linking on the exceptional divisor, color-tube threading, and Skein crossing changes.

Presentation of the particle Skein module. The Skein module admits the presentation

  \mathrm{Sk}_q(\mathbf{C}) = 
  \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]\bigl\langle
    \mathcal{G},
    \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}},
    \ell_c
  \bigr\rangle
  \Big/
  \bigl(
    qL_+ - q^{-1}L_- - (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})L_0
  \bigr),

where \mathcal{G} is the torus knot generator set. The quotient applies the HOMFLY-PT Skein relation at every crossing. Every particle in the knot--particle dictionary is a word in this presentation.
sec:skein-particle-generation-knot-parti: Having established that torus links T(m, n) generate the hadron monoid under skein resolution, one formalizes the bijection between prime knot classes embedded in \Sigma_4 and elementary particle states, and records the visual and algebraic inventory of binding knots used across the flavor and mass chapters.
rem:knot-particle-generation-interpretat:
Remark Hopf linking, color-tube threading, and Skein crossing change operations. Operation 1: Hopf linking on the exceptional divisor. Let \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2 be the exceptional divisor at a blow-up point c. The Hopf fibration S^3 \to S^2 \cong \mathcal{S}_c makes the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} the canonical linking on \mathcal{S}_c. Given two generators T_{m_1,n_1} and T_{m_2,n_2}, their Hopf linking is

  \ell_H  \colon 
  T_{m_1,n_1}, T_{m_2,n_2}
   \longmapsto 
  T_{m_1,n_1} \mathbin{\cup_{\mathrm{Hopf}}} T_{m_2,n_2},

producing a two-component link in S^3 fibered over \mathcal{S}_c. This is the colorless U(1) binding operation:

  • Degree 0: A single unknot T_{1,0} sits on \mathcal{S}_c with trivial braiding, corresponding to the neutrino at rest.
  • Degree 1: An excited unknot T_{1,0} at Reeb degree \deg\alpha_V = 1 acquires a unit of vertical charge.
  • Linking: Two such unknots Hopf-link on \mathcal{S}_c, producing the simplest non-trivial bound state. The Hopf link contributes a binding energy \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) invisible to the \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) base but detectable via the Skein polynomial.

Iterating Hopf linking builds the leptonic and mesonic sectors.

Operation 2: Color-tube threading. The three color tubes (r, g, b) = (w_2 - z, w_3 - z, w_4 - z) from Bring's surface provide a second linking operation. Given three generators T_{m_1,n_1}, T_{m_2,n_2}, T_{m_3,n_3}, their color-tube linking threads each knot through one of the three chiral fibers:

  \ell_c  \colon 
  T_{m_1,n_1}, T_{m_2,n_2}, T_{m_3,n_3}
   \longmapsto 
  T_{m_1,n_1} \mathbin{\cup_r} T_{m_2,n_2}
  \mathbin{\cup_g} T_{m_3,n_3}.

The S_3 \subset S_5 permutation symmetry of the color coordinates ensures this linking is invariant under color permutations. This reproduces the \mathrm{SU}(3) color confinement condition. Only color-singlet combinations produce observable hadrons.

Operation 3: Skein crossing change. The q-deformed Skein relation at a crossing

  q  L_+ -  q^{-1} L_-
  =  (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}) L_0

acts as a transmutation operation. Resolving or introducing crossings in a linked configuration converts torus topologies into hyperbolic ones. The figure-eight knot 4_1 (muon) is not a generator. It arises from a crossing change on a linked trefoil pair:

  T_{2,3} \mathbin{\cup_{\mathrm{Hopf}}} T_{2,3}
  \xrightarrow{\sigma}
  4_1 +  \text{(Skein remainder)}.

The muon is a Skein excitation of the electron.
prop:knot-particle-correspondence:
Proposition Knot--particle correspondence via q-Schur--Weyl duality. Let V = V_{1/2} be the fundamental representation of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)), and let B_n act on V^{\otimes n} via the R-matrix braiding, through the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(R, q). By q-Schur–Weyl duality, V^{\otimes n} decomposes into irreducible summands labelled by the partitions \lambda \vdash n with at most two rows.

The Markov trace is a weighted sum of the irreducible characters,

  \mathrm{tr}_M \;=\; \sum_{\lambda} y_\lambda\, \chi_\lambda ,

and the link invariant of the closure \hat\beta is a normalisation of \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta). Every irreducible summand therefore contributes, with weight y_\lambda\,\chi_\lambda(\beta), to the invariant of every n-strand closure.

This is not a bijection between summands and link types. There are \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 summands, while for n \ge 2 the closures of n-strand braids include infinitely many distinct link types, for example the torus links T(2, k).
rem:knot-particle-correspondence-hadron-: Remark Localized knots and hadrons under the knot–particle bijection. In particular, the invariant of each localized knot (p, K) in a bundle is a weighted sum over the irreducible summands, \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda; no single summand is assigned to it. Hadrons correspond to tensor products of such summands bound by Hopf links.
rem:knot-particle-dictionary:
Remark Knot–particle dictionary. The localized knot framework assigns a topological identity to each fundamental particle. This dictionary is derived from the categorical braiding on V = V_{1/2}. The R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) endows V^{\otimes n} with a faithful B_n-action. The q-Schur--Weyl duality decomposes V^{\otimes n} into irreducible summands labelled by partitions \lambda \vdash n. By Alexander's theorem, every oriented knot is the closure of a braid \beta \in B_n. The Markov trace on the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) identifies each irreducible summand with a knot type.

Fermion--boson principle. In the T(2,n) torus family on the Bring's surface, the number of connected components is \gcd(2,n). Fermions (n odd) are knots (1 component, half-integer spin). Bosons (n even) are links (2 components, integer spin). Quarks are Borromean-linked unknots in the exceptional divisor.

def:interaction-sector-taxonomy:
Definition Interaction-sector taxonomy. The framework's interactions form three sectors — strong, electromagnetic, and weak — classified by the bar-involution parity of the sector's primary observable, the calibration its scale anchors to, and its coupling object.

Sector Primary observable Bar parity (q \mapsto q^{-1}) Scale anchor Coupling object
strong binding \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}, volume even (cosh channel) E_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) Borromean Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}); confinement-SDP duals
electromagnetic Coulomb energy, Hartree scale provably no pure channel (mixed at coupling and observable level) E_h = \alpha_{EM}^2\, m_e c^2 \alpha_{EM}^{-1} = q_0\,[9]_q\,[10]_q dressed by the Chern–Simons tower
weak \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, bar-skew channel P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} odd (sinh channel) CAL-2 (P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}, proxy m_\mu/m_e) bar-odd channel of the complex volume

The taxonomy is a total assignment, and it is proved that weak is the unique bar-odd-assigned sector, that strong is the unique bar-even one, and that the electromagnetic sector is exactly the one carrying no pure-parity assignment — which is itself a theorem, not an omission, as follows.

At the coupling level the electromagnetic cell is now derived. The quantum integer [n]_q is bar-even — invariant under q \mapsto q^{-1} — so in the bare coupling C(q) = q\,[9]_q[10]_q only the exponential prefactor moves under the bar involution, giving the exact decomposition

  C(q) \pm C(q^{-1}) \;=\; (q \pm q^{-1})\,[9]_q[10]_q .

The bar-even part of the electromagnetic coupling is the cosh-channel (strong-side) multiple and the bar-odd part the sinh-channel (weak-side) multiple of one invariant factor B = [9]_q[10]_q: the electromagnetic coupling is the full exponential mix e^{\lambda} B with \lambda = \ln q, sitting at the intertwiner point between the two pure channels rather than in either. At the aether anchor the odd-to-even ratio is \tanh(\ln q_0) \approx 0.10396 exactly for the bare coupling, and \approx 0.10356 for the Chern–Simons-dressed value, whose tower is not bar-covariant in a single parity (\hbar_q^2 \mapsto q^2 \hbar_q^2). The observable level follows: \alpha = C^{-1} carries the conjugate exponential e^{-\lambda} (odd-to-even ratio -\tanh\ln q_0), and the Hartree scale \alpha^2 the doubled e^{-2\lambda} (ratio -\tanh 2\ln q_0 \approx -0.2057). Moreover, under the nondegeneracy that holds at the real anchor (q^2 \neq \pm 1, B \neq 0), the coupling is provably neither bar-even nor bar-odd — the electromagnetic cell is not unassigned but provably admits no pure-parity assignment, in exact contrast to binding (pure even) and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta (pure odd). All of this is proved over any field.
def:fusion-process:
Definition Fusion process. A fusion process is a nuclear process P = (\mathrm{initial}, \mathrm{final}) — two finite families of subjects (Z_i, N_i) — that conserves the Hecke strand count \sum 3(Z_i+N_i), the proton number \sum Z_i, and the baryon number \sum (Z_i+N_i) between its two sides.

A fusion process is a rearrangement inside the strong sector of the interaction-sector taxonomy: both sides embed in the common Hecke frame H_{3A_{\mathrm{tot}}}, and the energy release is a difference of bar-even bindings. A process that conserves baryon number while moving proton number — β-decay n \to p on the subject side — is not a fusion process; that failure is the subject-side discriminator routing it to the weak sector.

The following are proved: the process \mathrm{D} + \mathrm{T} \to {}^4\mathrm{He} + n is a fusion process with common frame H_{15}; β-decay is not; and the Littlewood–Richardson support-contraction property of the D–T instance — inducing the four subjects' operator-selection active sets into H_{15}, the final support (23 of the 176 partitions of 15) is strictly contained in the initial support (47), so no H_{15} Wedderburn block becomes reachable by fusing that was not reachable before. The partition counts are reproduced by two independent computations of Littlewood–Richardson positivity, one of them via skew ballot tableaux.
rem:binding-knots-visual-inventory:
Remark Visual inventory of binding knots. One collects diagrams for the knots and links that act as binding operators across the QOU framework. Each entry shows the standard diagram (TikZ), its braid word in B_n, and its entry point in the binding pipeline. For per-particle context, see the knot-particle dictionary.

Trivial: the unknot

The unknot 0_1 = T_{1,0} is a single unknotted circle — the trivial element of every braid group. It carries zero crossings. Hence it has zero q-deformed crossing energy, \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \cdot 0 = 0, and its bare mass vanishes. It plays two disjoint roles:

  1. Neutrino \nu: a single unknot in H_1(q). Its mass arises entirely from Reeb-divisor coupling, not from the knot itself.
  2. Each quark inside the Borromean baryon: the three strands of \mathcal{B}_3 are individually unknotted. Only their joint closure is non-trivial.
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1, line width=1.2pt]
  \draw[->, >=Latex] (0:0.9) arc (0:355:0.9);
  \node at (0, 0) {\small $0_1$};
  \node at (1.6, 0) {$\equiv$};
  \node at (3.0, 0) {$\beta = \mathbf{1} \in B_1$};
\end{tikzpicture}

Hopf link (the "bowtie")

The Hopf link L2a1 = T(2, 2) is the simplest non-trivial link: two circles linked once. Its braid word \sigma_0^2 \in B_2 closes to two interlocked loops, giving a "bowtie" silhouette when drawn flat with a single crossing per loop. This is the categorical identity of the gluon (strong-force mediator).

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1, line width=1.2pt]

  \draw[->, >=Latex] (-0.6, 0) circle (0.6);
  % right ring (overlapping)
  \draw[white, line width=4pt]
    (0.6, 0) ++(165:0.6) arc (165:195:0.6);
  \draw[->, >=Latex] (0.6, 0) circle (0.6);
  \node at (0, -1.2) {\small $L2a1 = T(2,2)$};
  \node at (3.4, 0) {$\beta = \sigma_0^2 \in B_2$};
\end{tikzpicture}

The full torus-link family T(2, 2k) supplies the electroweak bosons: T(2,2) gluon, T(2,4) W, T(2,6) Z, T(2,8) Higgs.

Trefoil 3_1 = T(2,3)

The trefoil knot is the simplest non-trivial knot, and the canonical electron identity. Its braid word \sigma_0^3 \in B_2 closes to a 3-cusp shape with three over/under crossings. The crossing energy 3 \cdot \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \frac{3}{2}(q - q^{-1}) fixes the leptonic mass quantum.

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, line width=1.2pt]

  \foreach \a in {0, 120, 240} {
    \draw[rotate=\a]
      (0:1.0) .. controls (40:1.4) and (80:1.4) .. (120:1.0);
  }
  \node at (0, 0) {\small $3_1$};
  \node at (3.0, 0) {$\beta = \sigma_0^3 \in B_2$};
\end{tikzpicture}

The torus-knot family T(2, 2k+1) extends to the muon T(2,5), tau T(2,7), and beyond.

Figure-eight 4_1 — the mass mechanism

The figure-eight 4_1 is the smallest hyperbolic knot (\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.0299, the CAL-2 calibration anchor). Its braid word is \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} \in B_3. The alternating positive/negative crossings give amphichirality 4_1 \cong 4_1^{\,\text{mirror}} (invariance under q \mapsto q^{-1}). This property selects 4_1 as the Higgs / mass mechanism.

Borromean rings \mathcal{B}_3 = 6^3_2

The Borromean rings are three mutually linked circles such that removing any one frees the other two — no two are individually linked. The braid word is (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 \in B_3 (three strands, six crossings). The hyperbolic volume is \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G (twice the volume of a regular ideal octahedron, where G is Catalan's constant). This provides the three-quark confinement identity for the proton, neutron, and ^4He nucleus, and sets the binding-energy scale \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G \approx 3.7445 MeV.

sec:borromean-reidemeister-intro: The Borromean rings 6^3_2, realized as the closure of the three-strand alternating word \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 \in B_3, form a Brunnian link: the three components are bound into a single topological composite, yet removing any one component leaves the remaining two unlinked. This section adopts \mathcal{B}_3 as the topological carrier of a three-quark baryon, introduces the flavour-typed crossing operator and its Gröbner–Shirshov normal form in H_3(q), proves invariance under all three Reidemeister moves, and demonstrates that single-component closures carry fermionic half-integer spin parity while two-component Hopf closures carry bosonic integer spin parity.
def:borromean-baryon:
Definition Borromean baryon. A Borromean baryon is a hadron whose three constituents are unknots K_{0_1} joined by the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 and bound by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H:

  B = 
  \mathcal{B}_3(K_{0_1}, K_{0_1}, K_{0_1})
   \oplus  \mathcal{L}_H
rem:borromean-topological-confinement:
Remark Topological three-body inseparability. Brunnian property. The defining property of the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 is that every two-component sub-link is the unlink. The three components are topologically inseparable, yet no two are pairwise linked. Deleting any one of the three unknots in a Borromean baryon leaves a trivial two-component unlink. The topological binding of the remaining two strands collapses immediately.

Implication for topological isolation. An "isolated" component requires lifting one unknot out of \mathcal{B}_3. This configuration is unstable in the Borromean topology. The move that extracts one strand unlinks the other two: pulling on a single constituent produces three unbound unknots. This Brunnian property models a strict three-body inseparability.
conj:brunnian-property-of-borromean:
Conjecture Brunnian property of \mathcal{B}_3: every two-component sub-link is the unlink. Let \mathcal{B}_3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3 be the standard Borromean link, presented as the closed braid \overline{(\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3} in B_3. For each i \in \{0, 1, 2\}, let \mathcal{B}_3 \setminus K_i denote the two-component sub-link obtained by removing the i-th component. Then \mathcal{B}_3 \setminus K_i is topologically equivalent to the trivial two-component unlink U_2.

This formalizes the confinement mechanism. Removing any single component dissolves the binding between the remaining two. This is the defining property of Brunnian links [kawauchi1996]. The three-component binding is invisible pairwise: all three pairwise linking numbers of \mathcal{B}_3 vanish, while Milnor's triple linking number is \mu_{123} = \pm 1, since one delta move turns the three-component unlink into \mathcal{B}_3 and raises \mu by 1. For such links 2\mu equals Pontryagin's \nu-invariant of the characteristic map T^3 \to S^2, an honest integer when the pairwise linking numbers vanish [dgkmsv2009, Thm. A, §4]. Naive strand-deletion at the braid word level does not immediately yield the empty braid. Deleting any one strand from (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 \in B_3 removes the four crossings that strand participates in and leaves two crossings of opposite sign, \sigma^{+}\sigma^{-}, with exponent sum 0. The closure therefore has two components, and the opposite-sign pair cancels under a single R2 move, giving U_2 directly. The three deletions are related by the cyclic symmetry of the word, so the same count holds for each.
